payload.description:
`basicly install` on the engine path never installs the tracker's post-merge shard-folding hook. The kit file that defines it is vendored into the repo and then nothing runs it.

OBSERVED AFTER A SUCCESSFUL INSTALL of basicly v0.14.1 (tag e2451c95) into terminal:
  $ ls .git/hooks/ | grep -v '\.sample$'
    commit-msg
    pre-commit
    pre-push
  No post-merge. Install's own line says the same: "Activated git hooks for stages: pre-commit,
  commit-msg, pre-push."
  CONTROL: the three hooks above DID install, so the listing is not returning a blanket empty; the
  absence of post-merge is a real absence, not a bad probe.

THE KIT FILE IS PRESENT BUT UNWIRED
  .basicly/core/kit/tracker/install_hook.py:8    HOOK_NAME = "post-merge"
  .basicly/core/kit/tracker/install_hook.py:179  "Wire a post-merge hook that folds every pending
                                                  writer shard into the ..."
  The engine vendors this file and never executes it. Grepping the engine's own cli.py at e2451c95
  for install_hook / post_merge / post-merge returns only the TIER kit's installer and the
  pre-commit stage activation. Nothing names the tracker's.

CONTRAST CONTROL - THE ENGINE HAS THE MECHANISM AND USES IT FOR THE OTHER KIT
  src/basicly/cli.py:1446  TIER_HOOK_INSTALLER = .basicly/core/kit/tier/install_hook.py
  src/basicly/cli.py:1449  def cmd_tier_hook(...) -> runs that script as a subprocess, and it is in
                           the install step list, printing "== basicly tier-hook ==" on our run.
  So a kit hook CAN be wired by the engine; the tracker's identically shaped install_hook.py simply
  has no equivalent step. This is the same divergence as term-n3rzn: the standalone kit installer
  does the wiring and the bundled engine path does not.

SECONDARY: _setup_tracker SHORT-CIRCUITS
  src/basicly/cli.py:1168-1179. With a ledger already present it prints "Tracker ledger exists; left
  unchanged." and returns. So even a future fix placed there would skip every existing consumer -
  exactly the repos that have shards to fold.

IMPACT
  Not data loss: the fold reads both events-*.jsonl and pending-*.jsonl, so reads stay correct and no
  event is lost. The cost is that shards are never consolidated automatically on a pull. terminal is
  the case that cares, being worked from two machines on the same branch: a pending-main.jsonl
  arriving from the other machine sits unfolded indefinitely, and the trunk log stops being the
  readable history of the project.

CONTRADICTS THE UPGRADE BRIEFING
  The basicly session's item 1 stated install "adds a post-merge git hook that folds shards into the
  trunk and commits them". On the engine path it does not. Their v0.14.1 release notes should not
  claim it either until the step exists.

WORKAROUND AVAILABLE, NOT YET APPLIED
  The vendored script appears runnable directly:
    python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/install_hook.py --root .
  Not run here - installing a git hook is a repo-state change and belongs to the owner, and it should
  be a fix upstream rather than a local hand-wire that the next install does not know about.
payload.title: basicly install never wires the tracker post-merge hook so pending shards are never folded

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: Given a repo with an existing ledger, when 'basicly install' completes, then .git/hooks/post-merge exists and folds pending-*.jsonl into the trunk log. Positive control: .git/hooks/pre-commit, commit-msg and pre-push are present in the same listing, proving the probe reads the hooks directory rather than returning empty. Second control: the install output names post-merge among the activated hooks rather than only pre-commit, commit-msg and pre-push.

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value: Closed by the basicly v0.14.1 install. 'git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/events-0001.jsonl' now reports 'merge: union' and 'text: unset' where it previously reported only 'text: auto, eol: lf'. Install announced it: 'Added events-*.jsonl -text merge=union, pending-*.jsonl -text merge=union to .gitattributes'. Negative control: README.md reports 'text: set' and no merge attribute, proving check-attr discriminates rather than reporting union for everything. No hand edit to .gitattributes was needed or made.

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value: Fixed upstream in basicly v0.14.1 (c9e7025f) and confirmed here from a real install rather than from source. 'git check-attr -a .basicly/ledger/pending-main.jsonl' reports 'merge: union', where the pre-install baseline reported only 'text: auto, eol: lf'. Negative control: README.md shows no merge attribute. The basicly session confirmed the root cause independently - their own .gitattributes carried the pending rule only because it had been hand-edited during the sharding work, so the rule looked present everywhere they checked and was absent for every consumer. The per-branch bound this record argued is now in their SPEC.md section 4.0: a shard removes the conflict between branches, the attribute removes the one within a branch.

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value:
Arm 2 fixed in basicly v0.14.1 and verified here on the case the fix exists for. The install re-pinned 5 refs in each of .vscode/tasks.json and .github/workflows/basicly-gates.yml and announced 'your previous copy is at <name>.basicly-bak'. Both backups are byte-identical to copies taken before the install (diff -q, independent of basicly's own claim), so the recovery path is real and not just reported. Both are covered by .gitignore:56 '*.basicly-bak', so they will not be committed by accident.

Arm 1 (install CREATES a CI workflow where none existed) is deliberately unfixed and tracked upstream as basicly-5166glz, filed there as a decision rather than a defect: whether a plain install may create CI is a different question from whether it may re-pin it, and changing it silently inside a patch would be the same class of surprise this record objected to. That reasoning is sound and arm 1 does not affect terminal, which already carries the workflow. Closing here; the open question lives upstream.

Still outstanding on this surface and NOT covered by the fix: there is no 'install --dry-run', so the tracked-file edit is still one a consumer sees after the fact rather than before.

payload.description:
The basicly v0.14.1 install restored a markdownlint pre-commit hook, and basicly's own generated markdown fails it 62 times. The upgrade cannot be committed.

BLOCKED: `git commit` of the upgrade is refused by the markdownlint hook.
  markdownlint-cli2 v0.23.0 (markdownlint v0.41.0), 151 files linted, 93 errors.

THE HOOK IS NEW, ADDED BY THIS INSTALL
  git diff of .pre-commit-config.yaml shows markdownlint added as the first hook, plus a new
  no-comments hook, plus every entry changed from `uv run python` to `uv run --no-project python`.
  Our previous commits this session (6ccd6d4, 43a9b9e) ran nine hooks and markdownlint was not among
  them. So this is the v0.12.2 restoration finally landing, two releases late for us.

WHO OWNS THE 93 ERRORS
  62 of 93 are in files we must not edit - basicly's projected output and vendored core:
    .agents/skills/**, .claude/skills/**, .basicly/core/skills/README.md, AGENTS.md,
    .github/copilot-instructions.md
  ALL 62 are a single rule: MD060 table-column-style.
  24 more are MD022/MD032 in CHANGELOG.md, and every one is inside a section headed
    "### Commit delta (auto-generated)" - written by `basicly release`, not by hand.
  That leaves 7 genuinely hand-authored errors, all MD060: README.md x1, terminal-cheat-sheet.md x6.

  So 86 of 93 are markdown basicly produced, and 7 are ours.

OUR FILES WERE NOT TOUCHED BY THE UPGRADE
  `git diff --cached --stat -- README.md CHANGELOG.md terminal-cheat-sheet.md` is EMPTY. The content
  did not change; the enforcement did. MD060 is a newer markdownlint rule and our
  .markdownlint-cli2.yaml (dated 11 Jul) sets `default: true`, so a rule added upstream auto-enables
  with no edit from us. That is the mechanism.

WHY WE CANNOT JUST FIX IT
  Editing .agents/skills/, .claude/skills/ or .basicly/core/ is forbidden by our own overlay rules and
  pointless - `basicly skills-build` regenerates them on the next install. A fix has to come from the
  generator or from scoping the linter.

THE SCOPING ADVICE COLLIDES WITH ITSELF
  The same install printed: "Your repo drives its own linters or formatters. The managed core is
  tracked, so tooling scoped to the repo root will lint and rewrite it. Exclude .basicly/core/".
  But .pre-commit-config.yaml is itself rewritten by hooks-build - install said so in its own output:
  ".pre-commit-config.yaml was rewritten to update managed hooks; comments/formatting outside them may
  have been normalized." So the file we are told to hand-edit is one the tool regenerates. And the
  advice names only .basicly/core/, while 62 of the errors are in .agents/ and .claude/, which the
  advice does not mention.

NOT DONE HERE, DELIBERATELY
  No gate was skipped, weakened or bypassed. No --no-verify. The upgrade is staged and uncommitted
  pending a fix. The 7 hand-authored MD060 errors are ours to fix and are not the blocker.

REPORTED UPSTREAM to the basicly session for a decision on the 86.
payload.title: markdownlint hook restored by v0-14-1 fails 62 times on basicly generated markdown blocking the upgrade commit

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value:
Fixed upstream in basicly v0.14.2 (a5286d9d) and verified here. markdownlint went 62 -> 0 in one step over 151 files, exit 0, which was the sharp test agreed with the basicly session: a partial drop would have meant a real difference between our projection sets.

THE ZERO IS CONTROLLED. A planted table matching the defect shape - padded cells over an unpadded delimiter row - reports 2 MD060 errors, so the rule is live and enabled. Worth recording that my FIRST control was itself a false negative: I planted a table that was valid compact style, so it reported zero and proved nothing. The probe answered instead of the code, which is the fourth instance of that failure this week and the only one that was mine.

Upstream root cause, both theirs: three catalog sources wrote a padded header and padded cells over an unpadded delimiter row, so markdownlint inferred compact and objected to every padded cell; and two generators rendered an empty cell as two spaces where the rule accepts one. Re-enabling MD060 on their side immediately surfaced 166 more in docs/architecture/status.md from the same empty-cell defect in a second generator.

Our own 31 errors were fixed here in the same pass and were never upstream's: 7 MD060 from eight ragged tables in README.md and terminal-cheat-sheet.md, and 24 MD022/MD032 from twelve missing blank lines after a '### Commit delta (auto-generated)' heading. The changelog half was NOT basicly's emitter - confirmed independently against this repo, where no source file, script or workflow contains the string and the sections arrive via docs(release) commits. Both fixes whitespace-only, verified two independent ways.

Landed in 539d37b with all twelve pre-commit hooks passing, markdownlint among them. No gate was skipped or weakened at any point; the upgrade sat staged and uncommitted for as long as it was blocked.

payload.description:
Retro proposal, not self-applied. The positive-control rule as written can be followed correctly and still yield a false zero, because it does not say what the control must be built FROM.

WHAT HAPPENED, the failure this comes from
  Verifying that basicly v0.14.2 fixed term-fawxo, markdownlint reported 0 errors over 151 files. Per
  the existing rule I ran a positive control: a planted table I believed was ragged. It reported ZERO.
  Taken at face value that reads as "the probe is dead, distrust the zero" - the opposite of the truth.
  The control was wrong, not the probe: my table used one space either side of each pipe, which is
  valid `compact` style and therefore never an MD060 violation. I had built the control from what I
  ASSUMED the defect looked like rather than from the defect actually observed.
  Rebuilt from the real failing shape - padded cells over an unpadded delimiter row, which is what the
  62 real errors were - it reported 2 errors. The zero was then trustworthy.

WHY THE CURRENT RULE DOES NOT CATCH IT
  .basicly/core/fragments/decisions/external-facts.fragment.yaml:21-24 says to run a positive control
  that must return something, and that if the control is empty too the zero belongs to the probe. Both
  halves were followed. The rule treats the control as trustworthy by construction, so a wrong control
  is indistinguishable from a dead probe, and it silently converts a correct zero into a false alarm -
  or, in the mirror case, a broken probe into a clean bill of health.

  This is a DIFFERENT failure from the three basicly hit the same week. Theirs were the environment
  answering instead of the code - markdownlint merging a repo config even under --config, a globs: key
  overriding the filename on the command line, a hand-edited .gitattributes. Those are all "the probe
  read something other than what you pointed it at". This one is "the probe was pointed at the right
  thing and the control was the wrong specimen". The existing rule covers theirs and not this.

PROPOSED WORDING, to append to that bullet
  "Build the control from a failure you have actually observed, not from what you assume the failure
  looks like - a control that is the right idea and the wrong instance reports zero and reads exactly
  like a dead probe. Check the denominator moved too: if adding the control did not change the count
  of things examined, it was never examined."

  The denominator half is load-bearing and was what rescued the diagnosis here: the lint run went from
  151 files to 152 when the control file was added, which proved the file WAS being read and sent me
  to look at the table rather than at the tooling.

WHERE IT COULD LIVE - a decision, which is why this is filed rather than applied
  A. Upstream in basicly. The rule is theirs, in managed core we must never edit, and the refinement is
     general rather than terminal-specific. They hit three instances of the parent failure in one day,
     so they have the motivation and the reach.
  B. A local overlay fragment under .basicly-local/fragments/user/. Ours immediately, no upstream wait,
     but it then sits alongside basicly's version of the same rule and the two can drift.
  Recommend A with B as a stopgap only if the upstream answer is slow. Owner decides; the basicly
  session has already said they are keeping the observation, which makes A cheap to ask for.

NOT DONE: no fragment written, no core file touched, nothing rebuilt.
payload.title: retro: a positive control must be built from the observed failure not an assumed one

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: Given the external-facts guidance, when an agent reports a zero backed by a positive control, then the guidance requires that control to be built from an observed failure and requires the examined-count to have changed. Positive control for this record itself: re-running the markdownlint zero-check with a compact-style table must still read as inconclusive under the new wording, where the old wording called it a dead probe.

payload.description:
`basicly install` prints linter-scoping advice unconditionally, without checking whether the change is already made. In this repo one half has been satisfied for releases and the advice still appears verbatim on every run.

WHAT IT PRINTS, on v0.14.1 and again unchanged on v0.14.2
  "Your repo drives its own linters or formatters. The managed core is tracked, so tooling scoped to
   the repo root will lint and rewrite it. Exclude `.basicly/core/`:
     .pre-commit-config.yaml: add `exclude: ^\.basicly/core/` to each hook that scans the repo
     .ruff.toml: add `extend-exclude = [\".basicly/core\"]`"

DEFECT 1 - THE RUFF HALF IS ALREADY DONE AND HAS BEEN FOR A WHILE
  .ruff.toml in this repo already carries, with a comment recording why:
      extend-exclude = [".basicly/core"]
  So the advice names a change that is present. An install cannot tell a consumer who ignored the
  advice from one who took it, because it never reads the file. Evidence that it is genuinely
  satisfied, not merely present: `uv run ruff format --check .basicly/core/` exits 0, "54 files
  already formatted" - ruff is not rewriting managed core.

DEFECT 2 - IT ADVISES HAND-EDITING A FILE THE SAME RUN REGENERATES
  The v0.14.1 run printed this advice and ALSO printed ".pre-commit-config.yaml was rewritten to
  update managed hooks; comments/formatting outside them may have been normalized." A consumer who
  follows the advice writes an `exclude:` into a file basicly rewrites. Raised during the v0.14.0
  audit and acknowledged by the basicly session; still emitted unchanged in v0.14.2.

DEFECT 3 - THE PATHS NAMED ARE NOT THE PATHS AT RISK
  The advice names only .basicly/core/. The markdownlint failure that blocked our upgrade
  (term-fawxo) was 62 errors of which the large majority sat under .agents/skills/ and
  .claude/skills/ - also generated, also tracked, not named by the advice. That is now moot for
  markdown because upstream fixed the generators rather than shipping an exclusion, which was the
  right call, but the advice text still describes a narrower blast radius than generated output
  actually has.

IMPACT
  Low severity, no gate fails because of it. The cost is that every install ends with a block of
  advice a consumer cannot act on and cannot dismiss, which trains them to skim the tail of the
  output - where the genuinely new information also appears. In this upgrade the same tail carried
  "Re-pinned 5 basicly reference(s) in .github/workflows/basicly-gates.yml", which is a tracked CI
  edit worth reading.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT
  Read the files before advising: skip the ruff line when extend-exclude already names .basicly/core,
  skip the pre-commit line when the exclude is present, and say nothing when both are. If the advice
  must stand for a regenerated file, it should name what basicly will preserve across a rewrite
  rather than asking for an edit it may discard.

NOT OURS TO FIX: this is basicly's install output. Filed here because it is our observation; the
change belongs upstream.
payload.title: basicly install prints linter-scoping advice for a change this repo already made

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value: Given a repo whose .ruff.toml already sets extend-exclude = ['.basicly/core'], when 'basicly install' runs, then it does not advise adding that exclusion. Positive control: a repo WITHOUT the exclusion must still receive the advice, proving the check reads the file rather than suppressing the message unconditionally.

payload.text:
RE-TESTED ON v0.15.0 — THE FIX IS A DELETION. The advice never appears now, including in a repo that genuinely lacks the exclusion. Fully controlled differential, two fixtures identical except for one line, verified by recursive diff before running anything:

  v0.15.0, repo WITH extend-exclude        -> silent   (correct)
  v0.15.0, repo WITHOUT extend-exclude     -> SILENT   (WRONG, should advise)
  v0.14.2, SAME fixture WITHOUT exclusion  -> ADVISES  (positive control)

The control is what makes this a real absence rather than a fixture that never reaches the code path. v0.14.2 printed the full advice block in the identical directory where v0.15.0 says nothing, so the path is reachable and v0.15.0 suppressed it.

Not a --dry-run artifact either: the silent result reproduces on a REAL install, not only under --dry-run. Both were run.

Fixture fidelity matters here and the first attempt was wrong. I initially built bare git repos with a .ruff.toml and no .basicly/ at all; those would have been silent for the trivial reason that no core catalog exists, and I would have reported a false confirmation. Rebuilt by copying this repo's actual .basicly/, basicly.toml, .pre-commit-config.yaml and .ruff.toml, then removing exactly one line. Same class of error as term-2vkce, caught before it produced a claim.

So term-ip2wz STAYS OPEN. The condition it asked for is unmet: a repo without the exclusion must still be advised.

payload.description:
`basicly install --dry-run` reports the tracker-hook step as FAILING on a repo whose core catalog predates the engine, when a real install performs that step correctly. A consumer reading the preview concludes the post-merge fix is broken and refuses the upgrade — the opposite of what a dry run is for.

OBSERVED, running v0.15.0's dry-run against this repo at core catalog 0.14.2:

  == basicly tracker-hook ==
  usage: install_hook.py [-h] [--root ROOT] [--ledger LEDGER] [--uninstall]
                         [--dry-run] [--interpreter INTERPRETER]
  install_hook.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --command if command -v basicly ... --advice uvx ...
  the post-merge hook was not installed, so a merged shard stays unfolded; run `basicly tracker fold`
  yourself after a merge

MECHANISM
  --dry-run deliberately writes nothing, so it does NOT sync the core catalog; it printed
  "Would sync core catalog at .basicly/core: 0 new, 3 updated". The vendored
  .basicly/core/kit/tracker/install_hook.py on disk is therefore still the 0.14.2 build, which has no
  --command or --advice parameters. The 0.15.0 engine invokes it with both. A real install syncs the
  new kit first, so the new install_hook.py is present by the time the step runs.

PROVED IT IS AN ARTEFACT, not a broken feature
  A REAL v0.15.0 install into a throwaway fixture carrying this repo's actual .basicly/ reported:
    == basicly tracker-hook ==
    tracker: wrote post-merge in <fixture>/.git/hooks
  and .git/hooks/post-merge exists, 478 bytes, with the run-time resolver and no absolute path. So the
  feature works and only the preview of it is wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC WARNING
  The dry run exists so a consumer can decide before anything writes. This one tells them the single
  feature the upgrade was cut for - folding a committed shard - will not install. Had we trusted it,
  we would have declined a release whose fix is fine. It is a false negative in exactly the place a
  consumer is least equipped to check.

UPSTREAM ALREADY NAMES THE ADJACENT CASE, which is why this looks like an oversight rather than a gap
in thinking. The dry run's own closing line says: "A projection is checked against the core catalog on
disk, not the one this run would sync, so when the sync above names a new or updated file, the run
rewrites more than this names." That is the same skew, reasoned about for projections and not for the
kit hook invocation.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT
  Any of: run the kit hook step against the catalog the sync WOULD produce rather than the one on
  disk; skip the step under --dry-run and say it was skipped for version skew; or catch the argument
  error and report it as skew rather than as a failed install. The third is smallest and keeps the
  step visible.

NOT OURS: basicly's dry-run implementation. Filed from a consumer observation.
payload.title: install --dry-run falsely reports the tracker-hook step failing on a pre-upgrade core catalog

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
